post_title: What will Brazil's IPCA-15 monthly inflation rate be for November 2026?

question.title: What will Brazil's IPCA-15 monthly inflation rate be for November 2026?
question.description:
IPCA-15 is IBGE's "mini-IPCA" and the first inflation reading for each month: it tracks prices for households earning 1 to 40 minimum wages, using a collection window running from the 16th of the previous month to the 15th of the reference month, and is published roughly 11 days before the full IPCA. The November 2026 edition covers prices collected from 16 October to 15 November 2026, so price changes after 15 November do not enter the reading. IBGE's official calendar lists the release for 26 November 2026 (https://www.ibge.gov.br/calendario/conjunturais.html), two weeks before the full November IPCA (11 December 2026).

Recent IPCA-15 monthly readings: April 2026 +0.89%, May +0.62%, June +0.41%, July +0.06%, August -0.40%, September +0.70%, October +0.32%. The October print (released 23 October 2026, https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-news/2184-news-agency/news/48358-ipca-15-is-0-32-in-october) left the index up 4.15% year-to-date and 4.62% over twelve months, up from 4.47% in the twelve months to September and above the 4.5% ceiling of Brazil's inflation target (3.0% +/- 1.5 pp).

October surprised to the downside twice. The IPCA-15 came in at +0.32% against a Valor Data median of +0.44% (range 0.37%-0.50%) and a Broadcast median of about +0.44%; the downside came mainly from residential electricity, which fell after Aneel switched to the green tariff flag (no extra charge) in October, and Aneel kept the green flag for November, the second consecutive month with no surcharge. The full October IPCA, published on 12 November 2026, then decelerated to +0.14% (from +0.82% in September), below every estimate in the Bloomberg (0.18%-0.50%) and Broadcast (0.18%-0.40%) ranges, with residential electricity at -1.92% and airfares falling while food rose; 12-month inflation moved up to 4.63% and the year-to-date figure reached 4.10%. Food and beverages have been the main upward pressure inside IPCA-15: in October, tomatoes rose 24.54%, onions 13.63%, potatoes 10.96% and rice 5.80%, with the food group up 0.88%. For seasonal reference, the November 2025 IPCA-15 was +0.20%.

Expectations for November are not settled: at least one house (4intelligence) has flagged around +0.3% for the month and Fecomércio-RS projects +0.38% for the full November IPCA, but recent misses in both directions (September's +0.70% against a market median near +0.55%) show how much dispersion surrounds the first print of each month. The policy backdrop is an overshooting inflation path: the Copom kept rates on hold at its 4 November 2026 meeting, the Focus survey of 9 November 2026 projects 2026 year-end inflation of 5.22% and a Selic of 13.75%, and the next Copom decision is on 9 December 2026, after this question resolves.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the month-on-month variation of Brazil's [IPCA-15](https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/statistics/economic/prices-and-costs/17137-extended-national-consumer-price-index-15.html) (Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo 15) for the November 2026 reference period, as published by [IBGE](https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/statistics/economic/prices-and-costs/17137-extended-national-consumer-price-index-15.html) on 26 November 2026 (release scheduled for 09:00 Brasília time, 12:00 UTC). The resolved value is the percentage monthly rate IBGE reports for November 2026, at IBGE's two-decimal precision: if IBGE reports a rise of 0.32%, the question resolves as 0.32; if it reports a fall of 0.15%, the question resolves as -0.15. The 12-month accumulated and year-to-date figures do not affect resolution. If IBGE's IPCA-15 page is unavailable or has not updated, the figure in IBGE's Agência de Notícias release for the same edition, or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the IBGE figure, will be used; if the release is delayed beyond 26 November 2026, resolution waits for IBGE's publication.
question.fine_print: If IBGE publishes an erratum revising the November 2026 monthly rate, the value displayed on IBGE's IPCA-15 page at the time of resolution governs.
